To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of field survey data and satellite image analysis can be successfully applied to produce multiple spatial products (e.g. bathymetry, seafloor cover and change) at a high spatial resolution in shallow coastal waters.

(1) a combination of field survey data and satellite imagery can produce high resolution, accurate maps of bathymetry, seafloor cover and seafloor species composition; (2) a change detection analysis can be used to map changes in seagrass percentage coverage over time; and (3) the combination of these maps can be used to assess the health of shallow coastal ecosystems and the impact of environmental change on these ecosystems.

“The integration of field and Quickbird 2 data was effective in producing high spatial resolution and accurate bathymetry, seafloor and change maps for the shallow coastal waters of Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of remote sensing to the management of coastal environments.
developing a repeatable, cost-effective and reliable method for producing high resolution, multi-product maps of shallow coastal benthic habitats.
the development of methods and techniques for mapping and monitoring shallow water environments and benthic habitats, and the application of these methods in the Moreton Bay region.

this study has developed a repeatable method to map bathymetric and seagrass cover in shallow coastal waters using Quickbird satellite imagery.
the study demonstrates the ability to map and monitor bathymetry and benthic habitats in shallow coastal environments using high spatial resolution satellite images.

the methods presented in this paper are a significant improvement over previous methods and provide an accurate and consistent means for mapping bathymetry and benthic habitats and monitoring change in shallow coastal waters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to map bathymetric depth, seagrass cover, seagrass species and changes in these parameters at a spatial resolution of 2 m and an accuracy level that is comparable to that of the field survey data.

the use of satellite data in shallow coastal waters is a viable and cost effective option for mapping bathymetry, seagras cover, seagrass species and change, however, the use of field survey data is essential for accurate mapping and validation.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to map seagrass species, cover and change at a high level of accuracy and spatial resolution, using a combination of field survey and satellite image data.

the methods can be implemented in other similar coastal water environments, but will need to be calibrated and validated to the local field data and conditions.
the methods are repeatable and can be used to map and monitor shallow coastal environments.
a single satellite image and field survey can provide a range of spatial data products for management applications.
